name: Early-onset Anterior Polar Cataract

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Anterior Polar Cataract

criteria.description: Presence of a well-demarcated, central anterior polar lens opacity visible on slit-lamp examination
Visual acuity reduction noted in infancy or early childhood consistent with lens opacity
Positive family history of anterior polar cataract or similar lens opacities
No evidence of other ocular abnormalities or systemic syndromes causing cataract

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anterior polar lens opacity with early-onset visual impairment; family history supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily clinical; genetic testing may assist in familial cases

pathognomonic.notes: Distinct, sharply circumscribed opacity on anterior lens surface
searchTerms: cloudy spot at front center of lens
opacity on front part of eye lens

pathognomonic.notes: Visual impairment typically noted in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: vision loss starting early in life
reduced visual sharpness from young age

common.notes: Light sensitivity due to lens opacity
In cases with significant visual impairment
searchTerms: involuntary eye movements due to poor vision
eye shaking caused by vision loss
nystagmus from lack of visual input

common.notes: Misalignment of eyes due to poor visual input
Astigmatism or myopia associated with lens changes

occasional.notes: Opacity may increase in size over time
searchTerms: lens opacity getting bigger over time
redness and swelling in eye front

occasional.notes: Secondary cataract changes in some patients

rare.notes: Elevated intraocular pressure due to lens changes
Visual developmental delay due to cataract

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing central anterior polar lens opacity
Ocular ultrasound if lens opacity precludes fundus visualization
other: Visual acuity testing demonstrating early impairment

distinguishingFeatures: Opacity located at posterior lens capsule rather than anterior surface
Central nuclear lens opacity involving deeper lens fibers

redFlags: Rapid progression of lens opacity causing severe visual impairment
Signs of lens-induced glaucoma (ocular pain, redness, elevated intraocular pressure)
Presence of systemic abnormalities suggesting syndromic cataract
references: Shiels A, Hejtmancik JF. Molecular genetics of cataract. Prog Mol Biol Transl Sci. 2015;134:203-218.
